items.title: Verification reachability ratchet — every real gate has a measured path
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: check-windows-hide is not reached by build:check and exits 1 on 33 direct child_process imports, so the repo can report 327/327 while violating the machine-safety rule that prevents terminal storms. The broader graph also leaves check-mobile-runtime-contract, check-workflow-git-depth, and generate-pathways --check outside the authoritative run. Outcome: a founder or agent reading the headline test count can trust that these release, mobile, workflow-history, and machine-safety contracts actually ran.
items.recipe: Expand check-build-gate-reachability into a source-declared multi-family ratchet for build/check/generate/derive/enrich scripts. Mark lifecycle-only tools by scope, wire the four verified build/release gates into build:check, route all 33 raw child_process imports through scripts/lib/safe-spawn.mjs, and lock direct, nested, lifecycle-exempt, default-check, and red-gate cases with both-direction self-tests.

L1.recipe: Wire the four verified gates and repair the 33 raw child_process imports until check-windows-hide passes.

L2.recipe: L1 plus multi-family reachability, explicit lifecycle scopes for the six legitimate non-build scripts, and mutation self-tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus exact-argument reachability receipts, measured gate counts in build-check diagnostics, and a public-safe proof row that cannot outlive the source fingerprint.

executionLog.note: All 33 direct child_process imports now route through safe-spawn. The reachability ratchet measures 233/233 declared gates, exercises 11/11 bidirectional mutation cases, and the Windows storm guard passes.

items.title: Closed-day velocity drift proof — verify the 60-day Oracle without crying wolf
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: build-oracle-velocity-public --check is explicitly a dry-run and never reads api/ecosystem-velocity.json. Its moving 60-day edge made byte comparison unsuitable, so the public Oracle can flatten or lag while the check stays green. Outcome: visitors and agents asking how active the forge has been receive a feed whose completed days are cryptographically bound to Git history while today's still-moving count remains honest.
items.recipe: Add closedThrough and a SHA-256 fingerprint over stable date/count pairs to the feed. In --check, rebuild from current Git history, compare only overlapping days strictly before the open day, reject any closed-day mutation or missing stable date, tolerate today's moving count, and self-test open-edge tolerance, closed-day drift, window rollover, and malformed committed feeds. Remove the dry-run declaration and let the reachability ratchet require this gate.

L1.recipe: Compare overlapping closed days and fail on drift while ignoring the current day.

L2.recipe: L1 plus committed closedThrough/fingerprint evidence, rollover semantics, malformed-input refusal, and both-direction self-tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus per-day proof diagnostics, source-history completeness checks for shallow clones, and downstream Oracle freshness/abstention wiring.

executionLog.note: The public velocity feed now carries closedThrough plus a stable SHA-256 fingerprint. It counts full-log committer instants normalized to UTC, proves 59 completed days while tolerating the still-moving open day, and passes 14/14 drift, rollover, and time-zone self-tests.

items.title: Publisher promotion cadence contract — say when repository-fresh becomes production-fresh
items.why: PRE-VERIFIED: six content-bearing publishers commit with [skip ci], while only refresh-live-data dispatches pages-deploy.yml. This is deliberately bounded by the four-hour coalescer, but neither api/deploy-currency.json nor /status explains that a repository-fresh feed may wait for the next promotion. Outcome: a human or agent checking trust signals can distinguish fresh source data from live production data and knows the maximum scheduled promotion lag.
items.recipe: Add a public-safe publisherPromotion contract to build-deploy-currency with strategy=coalesced, maxLagHours=4, promoterWorkflow=refresh-live-data.yml, and an explicit no-deploy-per-observation rationale. Render the cadence on the Production deploy currency tile, validate the field contract and copy, regenerate dependent proof feeds, and capture desktop/mobile screenshots across every theme for the touched status state.

L1.recipe: Publish maxLagHours/promoterWorkflow in deploy-currency and render one status detail line.

L2.recipe: L1 plus schema/consumer contract tests, derived proof regeneration, accessibility-safe copy, and every-theme desktop/mobile visual receipt.

L3.recipe: L2 plus next scheduled promotion estimate and a freshness distinction for repository-observed versus production-observed feed timestamps.

executionLog.note: Deploy currency publishes the four-hour coalesced promotion contract and /status renders the maximum lag. Field contracts pass, dependent feeds were regenerated, and 28/28 desktop/mobile captures across seven themes were manually reviewed.
